_readme: Industry-specific outbound use cases. Each entry names a REAL call an outbound team in that industry makes, and binds it to one of the 9 conversation archetypes (the proven prompt engines in /prompts). 'playbook' is injected into the system prompt as the goal for that specific call, so the agent talks like the industry rather than like a generic template. 'fields' drive the Single Call variable panel. Add an industry by adding a key here — no code change.

Banking.label: EMI Due Reminder
Banking.desc: Courteous nudge before a loan instalment is due
Banking.playbook: Remind the customer their loan EMI falls due shortly. Confirm they are aware, offer the quickest way to pay, and capture a promise-to-pay date if they cannot pay on time. Never pressure: this is a courtesy call before the due date, not a collection.

Banking.label: Missed EMI Follow-up
Banking.desc: Compliant follow-up on a missed instalment
Banking.playbook: The EMI was missed. Understand why before asking for anything: job loss, medical costs and genuine hardship need empathy and a restructuring referral, not a demand. State late fees and credit-bureau reporting factually, once. Secure a realistic promise-to-pay. Respect all local collections rules on timing and language.

Banking.label: Pre-approved Offer
Banking.desc: Pre-approved loan, card or limit increase
Banking.playbook: The customer is already pre-approved, so lead with that: no fresh paperwork, funds or limit available quickly. Be concrete about the amount and the rate. Never overstate approval as guaranteed disbursal. If interested, book a branch appointment or a callback with a relationship manager.

fields.label: Key Benefit
fields.ph: e.g. rate from 10.5 percent, no documents

Banking.label: KYC / Re-KYC Pending
Banking.desc: Chase pending KYC before the account is restricted
Banking.playbook: Their account needs a KYC refresh to stay fully operational. Frame it as protecting their account, not a compliance chore. Name exactly which documents are missing and the secure upload route. NEVER accept an OTP, PIN, card number or full ID number over the phone. Offer a branch visit as an alternative.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. address proof and a recent photo

fields.label: How to Submit
fields.ph: e.g. the mobile app or any branch

Banking.label: Deposit Maturing
Banking.desc: Fixed deposit maturing — renew or reinvest
Banking.playbook: Their deposit matures shortly and will otherwise move to a low-interest account. Give the maturity amount and the current renewal rate. Offer to auto-renew, reinvest at a better tenure, or pay out. Retention beats a hard sell: if they need the money, help them take it.

Banking.label: Branch Appointment
Banking.playbook: Confirm their branch appointment and make rescheduling effortless. Tell them what to bring so the visit is not wasted, and which branch. Keep it under a minute.

fields.label: What to Bring
fields.ph: e.g. original ID and the passbook

Banking.label: Service Feedback
Banking.desc: Satisfaction after a branch or service interaction
Banking.playbook: Ask how their recent interaction went and capture a score plus one line of verbatim. If the score is low, do not argue or explain: apologise, capture exactly what went wrong, and route it. A detractor handled well is worth more than a promoter.

Insurance.label: Premium Due
Insurance.playbook: Remind them the premium is due and that cover continues uninterrupted once paid. Give the amount, the date and the fastest payment route. If money is tight, mention available modes (monthly, quarterly) rather than letting the policy lapse.

Insurance.label: Lapsed Policy Revival
Insurance.desc: Premium missed — revive before cover is lost
Insurance.playbook: The premium was missed and cover is at risk. Be clear and unfrightening about what lapsing actually means for their family. Explain the grace period and the revival route. This is protection, not debt: never use collections pressure. Capture a promise-to-pay.

Insurance.label: Policy Renewal
Insurance.playbook: Their policy expires shortly. Lead with continuity of cover and any no-claim bonus they would forfeit. If the premium has risen, explain why plainly. If they are shopping around, ask what they have been quoted before defending price.

Insurance.label: Claim Documents Pending
Insurance.desc: Chase documents holding up a claim
Insurance.playbook: Their claim is stuck pending documents. The customer is often mid-crisis, so be gentle and practical. Name exactly what is missing and accept alternatives where possible. If they insist they already sent it, believe them and have it traced.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. the repair estimate and FIR copy

fields.label: Claim Reference
fields.ph: e.g. CLM four four two one

Insurance.label: Surveyor / Inspection Visit
Insurance.playbook: Confirm the surveyor's visit for their claim. Tell them what needs to be available (the vehicle, the damaged item, documents) so the visit is not wasted. Rescheduling should be effortless.

fields.label: What to Keep Ready
fields.ph: e.g. the vehicle and original documents

Insurance.label: Cover Enhancement
Insurance.playbook: Offer additional cover that fits their existing policy: a top-up, a critical-illness rider, or family floater extension. Anchor on the gap in their current protection, not on the product. Be honest that cover is subject to underwriting.

fields.label: Key Benefit
fields.ph: e.g. 10 lakh extra cover for a small premium

Insurance.label: Claim Experience Feedback
Insurance.playbook: Ask how the claim experience felt, end to end. Claims are the moment of truth in insurance, so listen carefully to detractors and capture the exact failure point. Never defend the settlement amount on this call.

Healthcare.label: Appointment Confirmation
Healthcare.playbook: Confirm their appointment with the doctor or department. Mention fasting, reports to bring, or arrival time if relevant. Missed slots cost the clinic and delay the patient, so make rescheduling immediate and easy. Never discuss the medical reason on the call.

Healthcare.label: Results Ready
Healthcare.desc: Reports are ready — arrange the follow-up
Healthcare.playbook: Tell them their reports are ready and how to collect or access them. NEVER read out, summarise, or hint at a clinical result: that is the clinician's job. If they press for findings, say warmly that the doctor will walk them through it, and book that consultation.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. available on the patient portal

fields.label: Reference
fields.ph: e.g. lab ID nine one two

Healthcare.label: Medication Refill
Healthcare.playbook: Their ongoing medication is due to run out. Adherence is the goal: check they are still taking it, arrange the refill, and flag to a clinician if they mention side effects or have stopped. Give no dosage advice of your own.

Healthcare.label: Insurance Pre-auth Pending
Healthcare.playbook: Their cashless approval is pending on paperwork. Patients or families are often anxious and mid-treatment, so be calm and concrete. Name the missing items and the fastest route, and offer to have the hospital desk help directly.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. the insurance card copy and ID proof

fields.label: How to Submit
fields.ph: e.g. the insurance desk on level one

Healthcare.label: Health Check Package
Healthcare.playbook: Offer a preventive health check suited to their age group. Lead with early detection and convenience, never with fear. Make no diagnostic claims or guarantees. If interested, book the slot on the call.

fields.label: What's Included
fields.ph: e.g. 60 tests with a doctor consultation

Healthcare.label: Post-Discharge Check-in
Healthcare.playbook: Check how they are recovering since discharge and how their stay was. Two goals: catch anyone struggling and route them to clinical help, and capture honest feedback. Warmth first, survey second. Escalate any mention of new or worsening symptoms.

Hospitality & Travel.label: Booking Confirmation
Hospitality & Travel.desc: Confirm an upcoming stay or reservation
Hospitality & Travel.playbook: Confirm their upcoming booking and arrival time. Use the call to capture preferences (early check-in, airport transfer, dietary needs, occasion) which lift the experience and the spend. Keep it warm and brief.

Hospitality & Travel.label: Booking Change
Hospitality & Travel.playbook: Something about their booking has changed on our side: a room type, a venue, a closed facility. Say it plainly, apologise once, and lead with the compensation or upgrade you can offer. Guests forgive changes handled generously and remember ones handled defensively.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. the pool is closed for maintenance

fields.label: What You Can Offer
fields.ph: e.g. a free upgrade or a full refund

Hospitality & Travel.label: Upgrade & Add-ons
Hospitality & Travel.desc: Room upgrade, spa, dining or late checkout
Hospitality & Travel.playbook: Offer an upgrade or add-on ahead of their stay: a better room, a spa slot, a dining package, late checkout. Tie it to the occasion if you know it (anniversary, business trip). One clear offer with a price, not a menu.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. sea view and lounge access

Hospitality & Travel.label: Membership Renewal
Hospitality & Travel.playbook: Their membership or tier is about to lapse. Remind them concretely what they lose (upgrades, late checkout, points) and what they have earned this year. If they have not travelled much, offer a lighter tier rather than losing them entirely.

Hospitality & Travel.label: Post-stay Feedback
Hospitality & Travel.playbook: Ask how their stay was and capture a score plus one specific detail. Hospitality feedback is reputational: a detractor who feels heard on the phone often does not post the review. Route anything serious immediately.

Hospitality & Travel.label: Group / Event Enquiry
Hospitality & Travel.desc: Qualify a group booking or event lead
Hospitality & Travel.playbook: They enquired about a group stay, wedding or corporate event. Qualify the essentials: dates, number of guests, budget range and decision timeline. Book the site visit or the sales callback. Do not quote a rate you cannot honour.

fields.label: Interested In
fields.ph: e.g. a wedding function for 200 guests

Financial Services.label: Instalment Due
Financial Services.playbook: Remind them their instalment or SIP is due and ensure the mandate will go through. A failed SIP breaks compounding, so frame it as protecting their plan. Offer to help update the mandate if the account has changed.

Financial Services.label: Portfolio Review
Financial Services.desc: Book or confirm an advisory review
Financial Services.playbook: Confirm their portfolio review with the advisor. Set the agenda in one line so they see the value and turn up. Never discuss specific returns or give advice on this call: that is the advisor's remit.

Financial Services.label: Investment Opportunity
Financial Services.desc: New fund, bond or product offer
Financial Services.playbook: Introduce a product that suits their stated risk profile. Be scrupulously honest: markets carry risk, past performance guarantees nothing, and you must never promise a return. The goal is a booked conversation with a licensed advisor, not a sale on the phone.

fields.label: Key Feature
fields.ph: e.g. suits a moderate risk profile

Financial Services.label: KYC Refresh
Financial Services.desc: Update KYC to keep the account active
Financial Services.playbook: Their KYC needs refreshing or transactions will be restricted. Explain it as a regulatory requirement that protects them. Name the documents and the secure route. Never take an OTP, PIN or full ID number over the phone.

Financial Services.label: Maturity & Reinvestment
Financial Services.playbook: Their investment matures shortly. Give the maturity value and the options: reinvest, switch, or redeem. If they need the funds, help them redeem cleanly rather than pushing a rollover. Trust retains more assets than pressure.

Financial Services.label: Advisory Lead
Financial Services.desc: Qualify a wealth or advisory enquiry
Financial Services.playbook: They enquired about financial advice. Qualify politely: what they want to achieve, rough investable amount, and timeline. Do not push for precise figures on a first call. The outcome is a booked meeting with a licensed advisor.

Retail.label: Order Delay
Retail.desc: Order delayed, split or out of stock
Retail.playbook: Their order will not arrive as promised. Say so immediately with the new date. Offer the real choices: wait, swap for an available alternative, or refund. Do not make them ask for the refund option, and never blame the courier.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. the item is out of stock at the hub

fields.label: Options
fields.ph: e.g. wait, swap, or a full refund

fields.label: Order Number
fields.ph: e.g. order four nine two one

Retail.label: Delivery Slot
Retail.desc: Confirm the delivery or installation window
Retail.playbook: Confirm the delivery or installation window and that someone will be there. A failed delivery costs more than this call. Capture any access instructions, and reschedule instantly if the slot no longer works.

Retail.label: Payment Failed
Retail.desc: Order held because payment did not go through
Retail.playbook: Their payment failed so the order is on hold. Be reassuring: nothing is lost and the items are reserved for a short window. Guide them to retry through the app or link. NEVER take card details, CVV or an OTP over the phone.

Retail.label: Abandoned Cart Win-back
Retail.playbook: They left items in their basket. Do not be creepy about it: mention the category rather than reciting their browsing. Ask if something stopped them (price, sizing, delivery time) and solve that. A modest incentive only if needed.

fields.label: Items
fields.ph: e.g. the items you were looking at

Retail.label: Membership Renewal
Retail.playbook: Their membership is expiring. Quantify what they actually saved this year in delivery fees and member prices: that number sells the renewal better than any pitch. If they shop rarely, offer the lower tier instead of losing them.

Retail.label: Purchase Feedback
Retail.desc: Feedback after a purchase or delivery
Retail.playbook: Ask about the product and the delivery separately: they fail for different reasons. Capture a score and one specific comment. If they are unhappy, resolve or route it there and then rather than just logging a number.

Manufacturing.label: Invoice Due
Manufacturing.desc: B2B invoice approaching its due date
Manufacturing.playbook: A business call to accounts payable, not a consumer call. Reference the invoice and PO number, confirm it is approved and scheduled for payment, and identify any blocker (missing GRN, mismatch, approval pending). Efficient and professional.

fields.label: Invoice / PO
fields.ph: e.g. invoice one nine four two

Manufacturing.label: Overdue Receivable
Manufacturing.playbook: The invoice is past due. Stay commercial and relationship-preserving: find out whether this is a process delay or a dispute, because they need very different handling. Get a committed payment date and the name of who owns it. Mention credit holds factually, never as a threat.

fields.label: Invoice
fields.ph: e.g. invoice one nine four two

fields.label: Consequence
fields.ph: e.g. a hold on new dispatches

Manufacturing.label: Dispatch / Production Delay
Manufacturing.desc: Order or shipment will miss its date
Manufacturing.playbook: Their order will not ship on time. B2B customers plan production around this, so give the revised date first and the reason second. Offer partial dispatch if it helps their line keep running. Never over-promise a recovery date you cannot hold.

fields.label: Options
fields.ph: e.g. partial dispatch now, balance next week

Manufacturing.label: Quotation Follow-up
Manufacturing.desc: Follow up on a quote or RFQ
Manufacturing.playbook: Follow up on the quotation sent. Establish where it sits: under technical evaluation, price comparison, or budget approval. Ask what would need to change to win it. Identify the actual decision maker and the timeline.

fields.label: Product Enquired
fields.ph: e.g. 200 units of the industrial pump

Manufacturing.label: AMC / Contract Renewal
Manufacturing.playbook: Their annual maintenance contract is expiring. Lead with uptime and response-time guarantees, and what an unplanned breakdown would cost them versus the contract. Quantify the service calls they used this year.

Manufacturing.label: Site / Service Visit
Manufacturing.desc: Confirm an engineer or site visit
Manufacturing.playbook: Confirm the engineer's visit. Check site access, safety induction requirements, and that the machine will be available and shut down if needed. A wasted engineer visit is expensive for both sides.

fields.label: Site Requirements
fields.ph: e.g. safety induction and machine shutdown

Education.label: Fee Due
Education.desc: Term or semester fee approaching due date
Education.playbook: Remind the parent or student that the fee instalment is due. Be respectful: fees are a sensitive family matter. Give the amount, the date, and the payment routes. Mention instalment options if the institution offers them.

Education.label: Overdue Fee
Education.desc: Follow up on an unpaid fee
Education.playbook: The fee is overdue. Handle with real care: never involve or shame the student, and never imply exclusion from class as a threat. Understand the family's situation, mention any hardship or instalment scheme, and secure a realistic date.

Education.label: Admission Documents
Education.desc: Documents pending to confirm a seat
Education.playbook: Their admission is confirmed but documents are pending, and the seat is at risk. Frame it as protecting the seat they have earned. Name exactly what is missing, the deadline, and whether scans are acceptable or originals are required.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. the class 12 marksheet and transfer certificate

fields.label: How to Submit
fields.ph: e.g. the admissions office or portal

Education.label: Counselling Session
Education.desc: Confirm a counselling or orientation slot
Education.playbook: Confirm their counselling, orientation or parent-teacher slot. Say what will be covered so they see the value and attend, and what to bring. Make rescheduling easy.

Education.label: Course Enquiry
Education.playbook: They enquired about a programme. Qualify gently: which course, their current qualification, intended intake, and whether they need scholarship or loan guidance. Never guarantee admission or a scholarship. Book the counselling session.

Education.label: Re-enrolment
Education.desc: Continue into the next term or year
Education.playbook: Confirm they are continuing into the next term. If they are hesitating, find out why: academics, fees, distance or a competing offer. Each needs a different response, and the counsellor or head can often resolve it if you surface it.

Education.label: Student / Parent Feedback
Education.playbook: Ask how the term has gone: teaching, support and facilities. Capture a score and one specific comment. Anything about safety, harassment or a student in distress must be escalated immediately, never merely logged.

Logistics.label: Delivery Window
Logistics.desc: Confirm the delivery slot and access
Logistics.playbook: Confirm the delivery window and that someone will receive it. Capture gate codes, floor, and alternate recipients. A first-attempt delivery is the single biggest cost saver in last-mile, so make it easy to change the slot now rather than fail tomorrow.

fields.label: Tracking Number
fields.ph: e.g. AWB four four one nine

Logistics.label: Delivery Exception
Logistics.playbook: The delivery failed or is delayed. Give the fact and the new plan immediately. Common causes are address issues, nobody home, or a hub delay: identify which, fix the root cause on the call, and confirm the next attempt.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. the address could not be located

fields.label: Tracking Number
fields.ph: e.g. AWB four four one nine

Logistics.label: Cash on Delivery
Logistics.desc: Confirm a COD amount before dispatch
Logistics.playbook: Confirm they are expecting the shipment and can pay the COD amount on arrival. This one call prevents a large share of refused deliveries. Mention accepted payment modes. Never collect payment details on the call.

Logistics.label: Address Verification
Logistics.playbook: The shipment cannot be delivered because the address is incomplete. Get the missing detail: landmark, floor, pin code, or a working phone number. Read the corrected address back in full and confirm before logging it.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. the flat number and a landmark

fields.label: Tracking Number
fields.ph: e.g. AWB four four one nine

Logistics.label: Delivery Feedback
Logistics.playbook: Ask about timeliness, packaging condition and the delivery agent's conduct. Capture a score and one specific comment. Anything alleging rudeness, damage or theft must be escalated, not just scored.

Logistics.label: Shipping Contract Renewal
Logistics.playbook: Their shipping contract is up for renewal. Lead with their actual service metrics this year: on-time percentage and volumes handled. If they are testing a competitor, ask directly what is being offered and on what lane.

Telecom.label: Bill Due
Telecom.desc: Monthly bill approaching its due date
Telecom.playbook: Remind them the bill is due and services continue uninterrupted once paid. Give the amount, date and quickest payment route. Offer auto-pay if they are repeatedly late.

Telecom.label: Overdue Bill
Telecom.desc: Unpaid bill heading toward service barring
Telecom.playbook: The bill is overdue and the line is heading for barring. State the barring date factually, once, as information rather than a threat. Understand the reason, offer instalments if available, and secure a promise-to-pay. Losing the customer costs far more than the arrears.

Telecom.label: Network Outage
Telecom.desc: Outage or planned maintenance in their area
Telecom.playbook: There is an outage or planned maintenance affecting their area. Give the window and the restoration estimate honestly. If you do not know the cause, say so. For business customers, mention any failover or hotspot option available.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. a fibre cut affecting your area

Telecom.label: Plan Upgrade
Telecom.desc: Better plan, data or bundled offer
Telecom.playbook: Offer a plan that genuinely fits their usage. If they consistently exceed their data or pay overage, say so plainly: the upgrade saves them money. Never upsell someone into a plan larger than they use.

fields.label: Key Benefit
fields.ph: e.g. double data for the same rental

Telecom.label: Plan Renewal
Telecom.playbook: Their pack or contract is about to expire and the connection risks going inactive. Give the expiry date and the fastest recharge route. If they are considering porting out, ask what is pulling them and offer the retention plan.

Telecom.label: e-KYC Pending
Telecom.desc: Verification pending on a new connection
Telecom.playbook: Their connection needs KYC verification or it will be deactivated by regulation. Explain it is a regulatory requirement. Name the documents and the route: app, store or a doorstep agent. Never accept an OTP over the phone.

fields.label: What's Needed
fields.ph: e.g. photo ID and address proof

Telecom.label: Service Feedback
Telecom.playbook: Ask whether their issue was actually resolved, not just whether the agent was polite. Capture a score and one comment. An unresolved issue should be reopened on this call, not simply recorded as a low score.

Utilities.label: Bill Due
Utilities.desc: Utility bill approaching its due date
Utilities.playbook: Remind them the bill is due, with the amount and date. Offer the quickest payment routes and auto-pay. Keep it brief and neutral: utility bills are non-discretionary and customers do not need persuading, just reminding.

Utilities.label: Disconnection Warning
Utilities.playbook: The bill is overdue and supply is at risk. Utilities are essential services, so handle vulnerability carefully: if they mention medical equipment, elderly residents or genuine hardship, route them to the hardship or priority-register team rather than pressing for payment. State the disconnection date factually, once.

Utilities.label: Planned Outage
Utilities.playbook: Warn them of a planned interruption so they can prepare. Give the exact window and the restoration time. Advise practical preparation (charge devices, store water). Ask whether anyone at the address depends on powered medical equipment and flag it if so.

fields.label: When
fields.ph: e.g. Sunday, 9 in the morning to 2 in the afternoon

fields.label: Impact
fields.ph: e.g. no supply for about 5 hours

Utilities.label: Meter Reading / Installation
Utilities.desc: Confirm a meter visit needing access
Utilities.playbook: Confirm the meter reading, replacement or smart-meter installation visit. The critical point is site access: confirm someone will be present and the meter is reachable. A missed visit means an estimated bill and a complaint later.

fields.label: Access Needed
fields.ph: e.g. someone at home and clear access to the meter

Utilities.label: Efficiency / Solar Offer
Utilities.desc: Energy saving, solar or tariff switch
Utilities.playbook: Offer a tariff switch, solar package or efficiency programme. Anchor on their actual consumption and the monthly saving in money, not in units. Be honest about payback periods and never overstate savings.

fields.label: Key Benefit
fields.ph: e.g. cut your monthly bill by about 40 percent

Utilities.label: Service Feedback
Utilities.desc: Feedback after a service visit or complaint
Utilities.playbook: Ask whether the fault was actually fixed and how the field team behaved. Capture a score and one comment. If the problem persists, raise it again on this call rather than closing it with a low score.

Automobile.label: Service Due
Automobile.desc: Vehicle service due — book the slot
Automobile.playbook: Their vehicle is due for service by date or mileage. Book the slot on this call: pick-up and drop, estimated time, and rough cost if standard. Mention any free service remaining under warranty, which is a strong reason to come in.

Automobile.label: Safety Recall
Automobile.playbook: A safety recall affects their vehicle. Be clear and non-alarming: state what the issue is, whether the car is safe to drive in the meantime, and that the fix is free. Book the workshop slot on this call. Never downplay a safety issue to protect the brand.

fields.label: What It Means
fields.ph: e.g. safe to drive, but please book within two weeks

fields.label: Next Step
fields.ph: e.g. a free workshop visit taking two hours

Automobile.label: Vehicle Insurance Renewal
Automobile.playbook: Their motor insurance expires shortly. Lead with the legal requirement and the no-claim bonus they would lose by lapsing even briefly. Offer to renew on the call or send the payment link.

Automobile.label: Test Drive Lead
Automobile.desc: Qualify a showroom or web enquiry
Automobile.playbook: They enquired about a model. Qualify: which variant, buying timeline, whether they are exchanging a vehicle, and finance or cash. The goal is a booked test drive with a date, not a quote over the phone.

fields.label: Model
fields.ph: e.g. the SUV in the top variant

Automobile.label: Exchange / Upgrade Offer
Automobile.playbook: Offer an exchange or upgrade on their current vehicle. Anchor on the trade-in value plus the campaign benefit. Be honest that the final valuation depends on inspection. Book the evaluation visit.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. extra 50,000 on exchange this month

Automobile.label: Vehicle Loan EMI
Automobile.playbook: Remind them the vehicle loan instalment is due, with the amount, date and payment route. Courteous and brief. If they signal difficulty, capture a promise-to-pay rather than pressing.

Automobile.label: Service Feedback
Automobile.playbook: Ask whether the problem was actually fixed, the cost matched the estimate, and the vehicle came back clean and on time. Those three drive dealer satisfaction scores. Escalate any billing dispute immediately.

Aviation.label: Flight Disruption
Aviation.playbook: Their flight is delayed or cancelled. Lead with the fact and the new departure time, then the rebooking options, best first. Passengers care about their connection and their onward plans, so ask about those. Mention hotel, meal or refund entitlements if they apply. Never speculate on the cause or blame weather if it is operational.

fields.label: Flight
fields.ph: e.g. flight six one two to Dubai

fields.label: Original Departure
fields.ph: e.g. Tuesday at 9 in the morning

fields.label: Rebooking Options
fields.ph: e.g. the 6 PM flight today, or a full refund

fields.label: Booking Reference
fields.ph: e.g. PNR seven K nine two

Aviation.label: Check-in Reminder
Aviation.desc: Flight approaching — check in and prepare
Aviation.playbook: Their flight is coming up. Prompt them to check in, and cover the essentials: terminal, reporting time, baggage allowance. Catching a documentation or timing problem now is far cheaper than a denied boarding at the airport.

fields.label: Reminders
fields.ph: e.g. report 3 hours before, 30 kilos checked baggage

Aviation.label: Seat & Baggage Upsell
Aviation.desc: Seat, baggage, lounge or cabin upgrade
Aviation.playbook: Offer a pre-flight extra: seat selection, extra baggage, lounge access or a cabin upgrade. Match it to the trip — extra baggage for a long holiday, a flat bed for an overnight, lounge for a long layover. One tailored offer with a price beats a list.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. flat bed and lounge access

Aviation.label: Miles / Tier Expiring
Aviation.desc: Frequent flyer miles or tier about to lapse
Aviation.playbook: Their miles or tier status is about to expire. Give the exact balance and date, and concrete ways to use or retain it: a redemption, a qualifying flight, or a partner spend. Losing tier status is what frequent flyers actually care about, so lead with that over the miles balance.

Aviation.label: Travel Documents
Aviation.desc: Passport, visa or advance passenger details missing
Aviation.playbook: Their booking is missing required travel details: passport number, visa confirmation or advance passenger information. Without these they can be denied boarding, so be clear about that consequence without alarming them. Direct them to the secure booking portal. NEVER take a full passport number over the phone.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. passport details and visa confirmation

fields.label: Where to Add
fields.ph: e.g. Manage Booking on the website

Aviation.label: Post-flight Feedback
Aviation.playbook: Ask about the journey end to end: check-in, cabin crew, seat comfort and baggage delivery. Capture a score and one specific comment. If they had a disruption, acknowledge it before asking for a score — surveying an unhappy passenger without that reads as tone-deaf.

Government.label: Application Documents
Government.desc: Documents pending on a citizen application
Government.playbook: Their application is pending on documents. Citizens often find government processes intimidating, so be exceptionally plain and patient: name each document in everyday language, say where to submit, and confirm they understood. Offer to send the list. Never use jargon or section numbers.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. proof of residence and a passport photo

fields.label: Where to Submit
fields.ph: e.g. the local citizen service centre

Government.label: Office Appointment
Government.desc: Confirm a biometric or verification slot
Government.playbook: Confirm their appointment at the office or service centre. Say exactly what to bring and which counter, because a wasted trip is a serious burden for many citizens. Confirm the address slowly and offer to send it.

fields.label: Office
fields.ph: e.g. the district office, counter four

fields.label: What to Bring
fields.ph: e.g. original ID and the acknowledgement slip

Government.label: Scheme / Deadline Notice
Government.playbook: Inform them about a scheme they are eligible for, or a deadline approaching. Be factual and free of any political framing. State clearly what they get, what they must do, and by when. Warn them plainly that no official will ever ask for money or an OTP for this.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. enrolment closes at the end of this month

fields.label: What They Get
fields.ph: e.g. subsidised cover for the household

fields.label: What to Do
fields.ph: e.g. enrol at any service centre

Government.label: Licence / Permit Renewal
Government.playbook: Their licence, permit or registration is expiring. State the expiry date, the renewal route and the penalty for lapsing, factually. Many people simply forget, so this call is a service, not a warning. Offer to send the renewal link.

Government.label: Tax / Fee Due
Government.desc: Property tax or civic fee due
Government.playbook: Remind them a civic due is payable, with the amount, deadline and any early-payment rebate. Give the official payment channels only, and state clearly that no officer will ask for payment over the phone. Keep it neutral and respectful.

Government.label: Service Feedback
Government.playbook: Ask how their recent service experience was: waiting time, staff conduct and whether the work was completed. Capture a score and one comment. Any allegation of a bribe or misconduct must be escalated immediately and never argued with.

fields.label: About
fields.ph: e.g. your recent visit to the office

Oil & Gas.label: Delivery Schedule
Oil & Gas.desc: Confirm a fuel or cylinder delivery slot
Oil & Gas.playbook: Confirm the delivery slot for their fuel, cylinder or bulk supply. Confirm site access, tank capacity or how many cylinders, and that someone authorised will be present to receive and sign.

fields.label: Access Needed
fields.ph: e.g. someone present to receive it

Oil & Gas.label: Supply Disruption
Oil & Gas.playbook: Supply is delayed or interrupted. For customers who depend on it for heating, cooking or running a business, this matters urgently. Give the revised date honestly, and any interim option: a partial delivery, a nearby depot, or priority allocation.

fields.label: Reason
fields.ph: e.g. a supply constraint at the terminal

fields.label: Interim Options
fields.ph: e.g. collect from the depot today

Oil & Gas.label: Safety Inspection
Oil & Gas.playbook: A mandatory safety inspection of their connection, pipeline or installation is due. Frame it as a legal and safety requirement that protects them. Confirm access and who will be present. Do not let them defer indefinitely: safety checks are not optional.

fields.label: Inspection
fields.ph: e.g. the mandatory gas safety check

Oil & Gas.label: Invoice Due
Oil & Gas.playbook: Remind the customer their supply invoice is due. For business accounts, speak to accounts payable and confirm approval status. For households, keep it simple and give the payment routes.

Oil & Gas.label: Subsidy / KYC Documents
Oil & Gas.desc: Documents needed to keep a subsidy active
Oil & Gas.playbook: Their subsidy or connection needs documents updated or the benefit stops. Explain simply what is needed and where to submit. Many affected customers are not comfortable with apps, so offer the offline route and the distributor's address.

fields.label: What's Needed
fields.ph: e.g. the linked bank account details

fields.label: Deadline
fields.ph: e.g. by the end of the month

Oil & Gas.label: Supply Contract Renewal
Oil & Gas.playbook: Their supply contract is up for renewal. Lead with reliability: delivery performance and volumes this year. If they are comparing rates, ask what they are being offered and on what volume commitment before defending price.

Call Centres.label: Scheduled Callback
Call Centres.desc: The callback the customer asked for
Call Centres.playbook: They asked to be called back at this time, so open by referencing that: it immediately separates you from a cold call. Confirm it is still a good moment, recap where the last conversation ended, and pick up from there.

Call Centres.label: Resolution Survey
Call Centres.playbook: Ask two things: was the issue actually resolved, and how did the agent handle it. Those are different questions and a polite agent who fixed nothing still counts as a failure. If it is unresolved, reopen the ticket on this call.

Call Centres.label: Collections Follow-up
Call Centres.playbook: You are calling on behalf of the client, so identify that clearly at the start. Follow the client's collections script and every local rule on calling hours, language and frequency. Understand the reason, offer the arrangements you are authorised to offer, and secure a promise-to-pay. Never threaten.

Call Centres.label: Lead Qualification
Call Centres.desc: Qualify and route an inbound lead
Call Centres.playbook: Qualify the lead against the client's criteria: need, budget range, timeline and decision authority. Be efficient without being an interrogation. The outcome is a clean handover with notes, or a polite disqualification.

Call Centres.label: Win-back Campaign
Call Centres.playbook: They left or went quiet. Open by asking what made them stop rather than pitching: the answer determines whether an offer is even relevant. If service failed them, acknowledge it before mentioning any incentive.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. three months at half price

fields.label: Valid Till
fields.ph: e.g. the end of this month

Call Centres.label: Verification Pending
Call Centres.desc: Chase documents on the client's behalf
Call Centres.playbook: Documents are pending to complete the customer's process. Identify who you are calling on behalf of. Name the missing items plainly and the submission route. Never accept sensitive credentials over the phone.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. photo ID and address proof

Mining.label: Dispatch Schedule
Mining.desc: Confirm a loading or dispatch slot
Mining.playbook: Confirm the dispatch or loading slot: date, tonnage and vehicle details. Confirm the transporter is arranged and documentation will be in order. A truck turning up on the wrong day blocks the weighbridge for everyone.

fields.label: Window
fields.ph: e.g. between 6 and 10 in the morning

fields.label: Requirements
fields.ph: e.g. transporter details and permits ready

Mining.label: Invoice Due
Mining.playbook: A commercial call to accounts payable. Reference the invoice and dispatch details, confirm approval status, and identify any blocker such as a quantity or grade dispute. Professional and brief.

Mining.label: Site Safety Notice
Mining.playbook: Notify of scheduled blasting, a haul road closure or a safety advisory affecting them or the neighbouring community. Give the exact window and the required precaution. Safety notices must be unambiguous: repeat the key time and instruction before closing.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. blasting in the north pit

fields.label: When
fields.ph: e.g. Thursday at 2 in the afternoon

fields.label: Required Precaution
fields.ph: e.g. stay clear of the boundary road for an hour

Mining.label: Offtake Contract Renewal
Mining.playbook: Their offtake or supply agreement is up for renewal. Lead with delivered reliability: tonnage supplied, grade consistency and on-time dispatch this year. Understand their volume outlook for next year before discussing price.

Mining.label: Compliance Documents
Mining.playbook: Compliance documents are outstanding: permits, transport authorisations or environmental clearances. Dispatch cannot proceed without them. Name each document precisely, since these are formal instruments, and confirm the submission route.

Mining.label: Community Feedback
Mining.playbook: Ask residents near the site about noise, dust, traffic and any community programme. This is a social licence to operate call: listen far more than you speak, never dismiss a concern, and route every complaint to the community relations team with the detail intact.

Non-Profit.label: Pledge Reminder
Non-Profit.desc: Gentle reminder on a pledged donation
Non-Profit.playbook: Remind them of the donation they pledged. Gratitude first, always: thank them before mentioning the amount. Give the simplest way to complete it. If circumstances have changed, accept that graciously and without a hint of guilt.

Non-Profit.label: Monthly Giving Renewal
Non-Profit.desc: Recurring donation lapsing or mandate failing
Non-Profit.playbook: Their recurring gift has lapsed or the mandate failed. Lead with impact: what their giving achieved this year, specifically. Offer to restart at the same level, or lower if money is tight. A smaller continuing gift is worth far more than a lost donor.

Non-Profit.label: Campaign Appeal
Non-Profit.playbook: Introduce a specific appeal. Be concrete about what a given amount actually does, since specificity raises giving far more than emotion does. Never pressure, never imply obligation, and thank them warmly whatever they decide.

fields.label: Impact
fields.ph: e.g. 2000 provides a family kit for a week

fields.label: Appeal Closes
fields.ph: e.g. the end of the month

Non-Profit.label: Volunteer Shift
Non-Profit.playbook: Confirm their volunteering shift: date, place and what to bring or wear. Volunteers are giving their time freely, so the tone is appreciative throughout. Make it effortless to change the shift without any awkwardness.

Non-Profit.label: Donor Feedback
Non-Profit.desc: How donors feel about impact reporting
Non-Profit.playbook: Thank them, share one concrete outcome their support enabled, then ask how well they feel informed about the impact. Donor retention rests on feeling connected to results. Capture what they would like to hear more about.

Non-Profit.label: Beneficiary Documents
Non-Profit.playbook: Documents are needed to process their assistance. Beneficiaries may be in distress or have limited literacy, so speak slowly, use everyday words, and confirm understanding. Offer help through a field worker rather than assuming they can upload anything.

fields.label: What's Needed
fields.ph: e.g. an ID copy and the bank passbook

Food & Beverage.label: Reservation Confirmation
Food & Beverage.playbook: Confirm the table booking: date, time and party size. No-shows are the single biggest cost in restaurants, so make cancelling easy and guilt-free rather than pushing them to keep it. Capture the occasion and any dietary or allergy requirement.

fields.label: Notes
fields.ph: e.g. table for four, one vegetarian

Food & Beverage.label: Order Delay
Food & Beverage.desc: Order running late or item unavailable
Food & Beverage.playbook: Their order is delayed or an item is unavailable. Tell them immediately with a realistic new time. Offer a substitute or a refund on that item without making them ask. Hungry customers forgive honesty and punish silence.

fields.label: What Happened
fields.ph: e.g. a delay on your order

fields.label: Options
fields.ph: e.g. a substitute dish or a refund on that item

Food & Beverage.label: Loyalty Offer
Food & Beverage.playbook: Offer a promotion suited to how they usually order: a weekday lunch deal for an office regular, a family bundle for weekend orders. Reference their usual preference lightly, never in a way that feels surveilled. Keep it to one offer.

Food & Beverage.label: Meal Plan Renewal
Food & Beverage.playbook: Their meal plan is ending. Ask how the food and delivery timing worked for them before pitching the renewal, since menu fatigue is the usual reason people stop. Offer a menu change or a smaller plan rather than losing them.

Food & Beverage.label: Dining Feedback
Food & Beverage.desc: Feedback after a visit or delivery
Food & Beverage.playbook: Ask about food quality, service and value separately. Capture a score and one specific comment. Any complaint about hygiene, an allergen error or illness must be escalated immediately as a safety issue, never handled as ordinary feedback.

Food & Beverage.label: Catering Enquiry
Food & Beverage.desc: Qualify an event or catering lead
Food & Beverage.playbook: They enquired about catering or a private event. Qualify: date, guest count, cuisine preference, budget per head and venue. Book the tasting or the callback with the events team. Do not quote a final price without the details confirmed.

fields.label: Event
fields.ph: e.g. an office party for 60 people

Entertainment.label: Event Reminder
Entertainment.playbook: Remind them of the upcoming event: date, venue, gate time and what to bring. Cover the practicalities that cause problems at the door — ticket format, ID requirements, parking. Keep the tone excited, not administrative.

fields.label: Venue
fields.ph: e.g. the city arena, gate four

fields.label: Reminders
fields.ph: e.g. bring photo ID and the digital ticket

Entertainment.label: Event Change
Entertainment.playbook: The event has been postponed, moved or cancelled. Give the fact and the new date or venue immediately, then the options: attend the new date, exchange, or refund. Fans are emotionally invested, so acknowledge the disappointment genuinely before moving to logistics.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. moved to the 26th, same venue

fields.label: Options
fields.ph: e.g. keep your seats, exchange, or a full refund

Entertainment.label: Subscription Renewal
Entertainment.playbook: Their subscription or season pass is expiring. Reference what is coming up that they would miss. If they have barely used it, offer a cheaper tier or a pause rather than a renewal they will resent and cancel anyway.

Entertainment.label: Presale / Ticket Offer
Entertainment.playbook: Offer early access or an upgrade: better seats, a fan package, a presale window. Genuine scarcity is fine to mention if it is real, but never invent urgency. Give the price and how long the window stays open.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. front block seats before general sale

Entertainment.label: Event Feedback
Entertainment.playbook: Ask about the event itself and the experience around it: entry queues, seating, sound and facilities. Capture a score and one comment. Escalate anything about crowd safety or staff conduct immediately.

Entertainment.label: Payment Failed
Entertainment.desc: Subscription payment did not go through
Entertainment.playbook: Their subscription payment failed and access will pause. Be reassuring: their account, watchlist and history are intact. Guide them to update the payment method through the app. NEVER take card details over the phone.

Construction & Real Estate.label: Site Visit
Construction & Real Estate.desc: Confirm a property or site viewing
Construction & Real Estate.playbook: Confirm the site or property visit: time, exact location and who will meet them. Directions matter, since sites are often hard to find. Mention safety requirements for an active construction site.

fields.label: Notes
fields.ph: e.g. closed shoes required on site

Construction & Real Estate.label: Milestone Payment Due
Construction & Real Estate.playbook: A construction-linked instalment is due because a milestone has been reached. Say which milestone was completed, since that is what justifies the demand. Give the amount, due date and payment route, plus the bank details process if a loan disbursal is involved.

Construction & Real Estate.label: Overdue Instalment
Construction & Real Estate.desc: Follow up on an overdue instalment
Construction & Real Estate.playbook: The instalment is overdue. These are large sums and the delay is often a loan disbursal problem rather than unwillingness, so diagnose that first and offer to coordinate with the bank. State interest on delayed payment factually, once.

Construction & Real Estate.label: Possession / Handover Update
Construction & Real Estate.playbook: Update them on the handover date. If it has slipped, say so directly with the revised date and the reason: buyers have usually planned a move, school admissions and loan timelines around this. Never give a date the project cannot hold, and explain any compensation clause honestly.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. approvals took longer than expected

fields.label: Unit Number
fields.ph: e.g. tower B, unit twelve oh four

Construction & Real Estate.label: Booking Documents
Construction & Real Estate.desc: Paperwork pending to complete a booking
Construction & Real Estate.playbook: Documents are pending to complete the booking or registration. These transactions are document-heavy, so name each item precisely and say which need originals or notarisation. Offer to have someone collect them if that is possible.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. PAN copy and the signed agreement

Construction & Real Estate.label: Property Enquiry
Construction & Real Estate.desc: Qualify a buyer or tenant enquiry
Construction & Real Estate.playbook: They enquired about a property. Qualify: configuration wanted, budget range, purchase timeline, whether they need a loan, and if it is for living in or investment. The outcome is a booked site visit, not a price negotiation on the phone.

Agriculture.label: Seasonal Input Offer
Agriculture.desc: Seed, fertiliser or crop protection offer
Agriculture.playbook: Offer inputs timed to the sowing or spraying window, which is when the farmer actually decides. Talk in terms of yield and acreage rather than product features. Be honest about what conditions the product suits, and mention any credit or instalment scheme.

fields.label: Benefit
fields.ph: e.g. suited to low rainfall, higher yield per acre

fields.label: Valid Till
fields.ph: e.g. before the sowing season ends

Agriculture.label: Crop Advisory
Agriculture.playbook: Warn them of a weather event, pest outbreak or disease risk in their area, and what to do about it now. This is genuinely valuable information, so be specific and practical about timing. Never overstate certainty on a forecast, and give the helpline for follow-up advice.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. stem borer reported in nearby villages

fields.label: Recommended Action
fields.ph: e.g. inspect the crop and spray within three days

Agriculture.label: Crop Loan Repayment
Agriculture.playbook: Remind them their crop loan repayment is due. Farm income is seasonal and tied to harvest and mandi sales, so ask about the harvest timing and align the repayment to it where the scheme allows. Mention any prompt-repayment interest subvention they would lose.

fields.label: Due Date
fields.ph: e.g. the end of next month

Agriculture.label: Procurement Slot
Agriculture.playbook: Confirm their procurement or collection slot: date, centre and expected quantity. Tell them what to bring — registration papers, quality requirements and moisture limits — because a rejected load after a long journey is a serious loss.

fields.label: Requirements
fields.ph: e.g. registration slip, moisture below 14 percent

Agriculture.label: Subsidy Documents
Agriculture.desc: Paperwork pending on a subsidy claim
Agriculture.playbook: Documents are pending on their subsidy or scheme benefit. Speak in plain local terms and avoid scheme jargon and section numbers. Name what is needed, where to hand it in, and offer help from the local extension officer.

fields.label: What's Needed
fields.ph: e.g. the land record copy and bank passbook

Agriculture.label: Farmer Feedback
Agriculture.desc: Feedback on inputs, advisory or procurement
Agriculture.playbook: Ask how the product or service performed on their field: germination, yield, or the procurement experience. Capture a score and one specific comment. Product performance complaints should be routed to the agronomy team, since they may indicate a genuine quality issue.

fields.label: About
fields.ph: e.g. the seed you bought this season

Pharmacy.label: Refill Reminder
Pharmacy.playbook: Their regular medication is due to run out. Adherence is the point: confirm they are still on it and arrange the refill. If they mention side effects, or say they have stopped taking it, do not advise — route them to the pharmacist or their doctor.

Pharmacy.label: Order Ready
Pharmacy.desc: Medicine in stock or ready for collection
Pharmacy.playbook: Their medicine has arrived or is ready to collect. Give the store, the collection window and how long it will be held. If it was a special order they have been waiting on, lead with that: it is genuinely good news.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. ready at the Anna Nagar store

fields.label: Held Until
fields.ph: e.g. for the next five days

Pharmacy.label: Delivery Slot
Pharmacy.playbook: Confirm the delivery window for their medicines. Check someone will be available to receive them, especially for items needing refrigeration or a signature. Confirm the address and any access instructions.

Pharmacy.label: Prescription Required
Pharmacy.playbook: The order cannot be dispensed without a valid prescription. This is a legal requirement, so be firm but helpful: explain what is acceptable, how to upload it, and offer to contact their clinic if they have lost it. Never suggest any workaround.

fields.label: How to Submit
fields.ph: e.g. upload on the app or bring it to the store

Pharmacy.label: Wellness Offer
Pharmacy.playbook: Offer a wellness product, health check or savings card. Stay strictly within over-the-counter and wellness territory: never recommend a prescription medicine, never suggest anything for a described symptom, and make no health claims. Suggest the pharmacist for anything clinical.

fields.label: Valid Till
fields.ph: e.g. the end of the month

Pharmacy.label: Pharmacy Feedback
Pharmacy.playbook: Ask about availability, delivery speed and pharmacist helpfulness. Capture a score and one comment. Anything about a wrong medicine dispensed or a suspected dispensing error must be escalated immediately as a patient safety matter.

Legal Services.label: Consultation Reminder
Legal Services.desc: Confirm a client meeting or hearing prep
Legal Services.playbook: Confirm the consultation with the solicitor. Say what to bring, since a meeting without the documents wastes billable time and delays the matter. Never discuss the substance of the case on this call, and never confirm to anyone else that the person is a client.

fields.label: What to Bring
fields.ph: e.g. the signed agreement and ID

Legal Services.label: Matter Documents Pending
Legal Services.playbook: The matter cannot progress without documents. Be precise about what is needed and whether originals, certified copies or notarisation are required, because a rejected document costs weeks. Explain the consequence of a court or filing deadline factually. Never give legal advice on this call.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. certified ID and the signed mandate

Legal Services.label: Fee Note Due
Legal Services.playbook: Remind the client the fee note is due. Keep it discreet and professional: legal bills are sensitive and the client may be under financial strain from the matter itself. Give the amount, date and payment route, and offer to have the partner discuss the bill if they have questions about it.

Legal Services.label: Overdue Fees
Legal Services.desc: Follow up on an unpaid fee note
Legal Services.playbook: The fee note is overdue. Handle carefully: the client relationship usually matters more than the speed of collection, and a disputed bill needs the partner, not pressure. Establish whether it is a cashflow issue or a query on the bill, and route a query rather than arguing it.

Legal Services.label: Case Update
Legal Services.desc: Hearing date, filing or outcome update
Legal Services.playbook: Update the client on a development: a hearing date moved, a filing completed, a response received. Say only what you are authorised to convey and never interpret it, since that is the solicitor's role. Clients are anxious about their matters, so be warm and offer to arrange a call with their solicitor.

fields.label: Update Type
fields.ph: e.g. a change of hearing date

fields.label: Next Step
fields.ph: e.g. a call with your solicitor this week

Legal Services.label: New Enquiry
Legal Services.playbook: They enquired about legal help. Establish the area of law, rough timeline and whether there is a deadline or court date, and check for a conflict of interest before anything else. Never advise on the merits of their case or quote an outcome. Book the consultation.

Legal Services.label: Retainer Renewal
Legal Services.playbook: Their retainer is up for renewal. Lead with what the firm actually handled this year and the value of having counsel on call rather than paying ad hoc. If they are reducing legal spend, offer a smaller retainer instead of losing the relationship.

Accounting & Tax.label: Filing Documents Pending
Accounting & Tax.desc: Records needed before a filing deadline
Accounting & Tax.playbook: The return cannot be filed without their records. Deadlines here are statutory and the penalties are automatic, so be clear about the date without inducing panic. Name exactly what is missing and offer the simplest route. Most clients delay because they are unsure what counts, so explain plainly.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. bank statements and expense receipts

Accounting & Tax.label: Deadline Notice
Accounting & Tax.playbook: Warn them of an approaching statutory deadline or a change in the rules that affects them. This is a service call that saves them a penalty, so lead with that. Be precise about the date and what they must do, and offer to handle it for them.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. the instalment falls due this month

fields.label: What They Should Do
fields.ph: e.g. approve the computation we sent

Accounting & Tax.label: Review Meeting
Accounting & Tax.desc: Confirm a year-end or planning meeting
Accounting & Tax.playbook: Confirm the review meeting. Set the agenda in one line so they see it is worth their time, and say what to have ready. Year-end meetings drive the advisory work, so getting them to attend matters.

Accounting & Tax.label: Invoice Due
Accounting & Tax.playbook: Remind them the invoice is due, with amount, date and payment route. Brief and professional. If they query the scope of the bill, capture it and route it to the partner rather than defending it.

fields.label: Invoice
fields.ph: e.g. invoice for the annual accounts

Accounting & Tax.label: Advisory Upsell
Accounting & Tax.playbook: Offer an additional service that fits what you already know about their business: payroll if they are hiring, bookkeeping if their records arrive messy, advisory if they are growing. Anchor on the time or penalty risk it removes. Never promise a tax saving.

fields.label: Benefit
fields.ph: e.g. books always current, no year-end scramble

Accounting & Tax.label: Engagement Renewal
Accounting & Tax.playbook: Their annual engagement is up for renewal. Lead with continuity: the same team already knows their business, and switching mid-cycle costs them time. If fees are the issue, understand what changed before discounting.

Accounting & Tax.label: Client Feedback
Accounting & Tax.playbook: Ask about responsiveness, clarity of advice and value for money. Those three decide whether an accountancy client stays. Capture a score and one comment, and route anything about a missed deadline immediately.

SaaS & Technology.label: Trial Conversion
SaaS & Technology.desc: Convert a trial before it expires
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Their trial is running. Find out what they actually tried to do with it and whether they got there, since a stalled trial is an onboarding problem, not a pricing one. Qualify team size, timeline and who signs off. Book a demo or hand to sales rather than discounting on the call.

fields.label: Interested In
fields.ph: e.g. the professional plan for 20 seats

SaaS & Technology.label: Onboarding Session
SaaS & Technology.desc: Confirm an onboarding or training call
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Confirm the onboarding session. Ask who else should join, since adoption depends on the whole team not just the buyer, and check they will have access ready. Say what will be covered so it feels worth the hour.

SaaS & Technology.label: Renewal & Churn Risk
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Their subscription is up for renewal. If usage has dropped, say so plainly and ask what changed, because a quiet renewal on a dying account just delays the churn. Offer a right-sized plan or fresh training rather than pushing the same tier. Escalate anything that sounds like a competitor evaluation.

SaaS & Technology.label: Payment Failed
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Their payment failed and the account will suspend. Be reassuring: data is safe and nothing is deleted. Usually it is an expired card. Direct them to update billing in the app. NEVER take card details over the phone.

SaaS & Technology.label: Incident / Maintenance Notice
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Notify them of an incident or planned maintenance affecting their account. Be factual about impact and duration, and never minimise. For business-critical customers give the workaround if there is one, and say when the next update comes. Do not speculate on root cause before it is confirmed.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. reports are delayed for some accounts

SaaS & Technology.label: Expansion Offer
SaaS & Technology.desc: More seats, tier upgrade or a new module
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Offer expansion grounded in their actual usage: they are at their seat limit, hitting an API cap, or asking for a feature that exists in the tier above. That evidence sells it. Never upsell an account that is not using what it already has.

fields.label: Why
fields.ph: e.g. you have been at your seat limit for a month

SaaS & Technology.label: Product Feedback
SaaS & Technology.playbook: Ask how the product is working for them and what one thing would make it better. Capture a score plus that verbatim, since the feature request is often worth more than the number. Route detractors to customer success the same day.

Fitness & Wellness.label: Membership Renewal
Fitness & Wellness.playbook: Their membership is expiring. If they have been attending, lead with their progress and streak. If they have not, do not shame them: ask what got in the way and offer a fresh start, a different class time, or a smaller plan. Guilt loses members; understanding keeps them.

Fitness & Wellness.label: Class / Session Reminder
Fitness & Wellness.desc: Confirm a booked class or PT session
Fitness & Wellness.playbook: Confirm their booked class or personal training session. No-shows block a slot someone else wanted, so make cancelling easy and early rather than pressing them to attend. Mention what to bring and the arrival time.

Fitness & Wellness.label: Lapsed Member Win-back
Fitness & Wellness.playbook: They have stopped attending. Open by asking what changed, not with an offer, because the reason is usually schedule, injury or intimidation rather than price. Match the solution to the reason: a different time, a gentler class, or a pause instead of a cancellation.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. includes a free session with a trainer

fields.label: Valid Till
fields.ph: e.g. the end of the month

Fitness & Wellness.label: Membership Dues
Fitness & Wellness.playbook: Their monthly dues are due or the mandate failed. Keep it light and quick, and offer to fix the mandate on the call. Access continues once it clears.

Fitness & Wellness.label: Schedule Change
Fitness & Wellness.desc: Class cancelled, moved or trainer changed
Fitness & Wellness.playbook: A class has moved, been cancelled, or the trainer has changed. Tell them early enough to re-plan their day, and offer the nearest alternative slot immediately. Members forgive changes; they resent turning up to a locked door.

fields.label: Alternatives
fields.ph: e.g. the 8 AM class or Thursday same time

Fitness & Wellness.label: Member Feedback
Fitness & Wellness.desc: Feedback on classes, trainers and facilities
Fitness & Wellness.playbook: Ask about classes, trainers, cleanliness and equipment. Capture a score and one comment. Anything about hygiene, injury or inappropriate conduct by staff must be escalated immediately, not logged.

Staffing & Recruitment.label: Interview Scheduling
Staffing & Recruitment.playbook: Confirm the interview: time, format, who they will meet and how long. Candidates often take leave to attend, so a clear confirmation matters. Check they have the joining link or the address, and make rescheduling easy without judgement.

fields.label: Where / Link
fields.ph: e.g. video call, link sent by email

Staffing & Recruitment.label: Candidate Screening
Staffing & Recruitment.desc: Qualify a candidate for a role
Staffing & Recruitment.playbook: Screen the candidate against the role: current situation, notice period, salary expectation and whether the location or shift works. Be respectful of their time and honest about the role. Never pressure someone into a role that plainly does not fit, and never disclose the employer before they consent.

Staffing & Recruitment.label: Offer / Status Update
Staffing & Recruitment.playbook: Update the candidate on where they stand. If it is an offer, be clear and warm about the details and next step. If it is a rejection, be brief, kind and definite, and give one piece of useful feedback if you have it. Candidates remember how they were told.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. the client would like to proceed

fields.label: Next Step
fields.ph: e.g. review the offer letter by Friday

Staffing & Recruitment.label: Onboarding Documents
Staffing & Recruitment.desc: Documents needed before a start date
Staffing & Recruitment.playbook: Documents are pending before their start date. Name each one and say which need originals. Be reassuring: this is routine and the start date is safe as long as it arrives in time. NEVER take a full ID or bank number over the phone; direct them to the secure portal.

fields.label: What's Missing
fields.ph: e.g. the relieving letter and ID proof

Staffing & Recruitment.label: Client Vacancy Outreach
Staffing & Recruitment.desc: Pitch the agency to a hiring employer
Staffing & Recruitment.playbook: Reach out to a hiring employer. Lead with a relevant placement you have made or candidates already on your books for that role, not with a description of the agency. Establish the vacancy, timeline and whether they are working with anyone else. Book a briefing call.

fields.label: Offer
fields.ph: e.g. shortlist for your open role

fields.label: Hook
fields.ph: e.g. three pre-vetted candidates available now

Staffing & Recruitment.label: Placement Feedback
Staffing & Recruitment.desc: Feedback from candidate or employer after a placement
Staffing & Recruitment.playbook: Check in after the placement: is the role as described, and is the new hire settling in. Ask both sides where you can. Catching a mismatch in the first month is what saves a placement and the fee.

fields.label: About
fields.ph: e.g. your first month in the role

Home Services.label: Service Visit
Home Services.playbook: Confirm the visit window and that someone over eighteen will be home with access to the equipment. A failed visit costs a whole slot. Confirm parking, gate codes and whether pets need securing, and give the technician's arrival window honestly.

fields.label: Access Needed
fields.ph: e.g. clear access to the unit, pets secured

Home Services.label: Service Due
Home Services.desc: Annual service or plan renewal due
Home Services.playbook: Their annual service or plan is due. Lead with what skipping it costs: breakdowns in peak season, a voided warranty, higher bills. Book the slot on the call rather than promising to call back.

Home Services.label: Technician Delay
Home Services.desc: Running late or needs to reschedule
Home Services.playbook: The technician is delayed or cannot make the window. Call as early as you know, because the customer has taken time off for this. Give a realistic new time, apologise once, and offer the first slot tomorrow if today is gone. Never let them wait without knowing.

fields.label: What Happened
fields.ph: e.g. a delay to your appointment

fields.label: Options
fields.ph: e.g. later today or first thing tomorrow

Home Services.label: Invoice Due
Home Services.playbook: Remind them the invoice for the completed job is due. Reference what was done so they can place it. Give the amount and payment route. If they raise a quality issue, do not push for payment: capture it and get the team back out.

Home Services.label: Quote Follow-up
Home Services.desc: Follow up on a quotation given
Home Services.playbook: Follow up on the quote. Find out whether it is price, timing or trust holding them back, since each needs a different answer. Offer to walk through what the price covers. Never badger: one good follow-up beats five chasing calls.

fields.label: Source
fields.ph: e.g. the site visit last week

Home Services.label: Job Feedback
Home Services.playbook: Ask whether the problem is actually fixed, whether the technician was punctual and tidy, and whether the price matched the quote. Those three drive reviews in home services. Any recurrence of the fault should be rebooked on this call.

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: End-of-Support Migration
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.desc: Platform going out of support — plan the move
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: A product, version or platform they run reaches end of support on a fixed date, after which there are no security patches. Lead with that date and what it means for their risk and audit position, not with a product pitch. Be precise and unalarming: this is a date on a roadmap, not a scare. Establish who owns the estate, whether they have budget in this cycle, and book the assessment. Never imply their systems will stop working on the date.

fields.label: Migration Path
fields.ph: e.g. upgrade to the supported release

fields.label: What's Affected
fields.ph: e.g. the version you run goes out of support

fields.label: Indicative Value
fields.ph: e.g. migration assessment at no cost

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Support & Subscription Renewal
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: Their support subscription is expiring. Be concrete about what lapsing actually costs them: no security patches, no entitled fixes, no upgrade rights, and reinstatement fees if they let it drop and come back. Reference the tickets and patches they consumed this year, since that number justifies the renewal better than any pitch. If budget is the blocker, surface a co-termed or multi-year option rather than losing the entitlement.

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Major Incident Notification
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.desc: P1 outage or degradation affecting them
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: A severity-one incident is affecting their service. Call early, even without a root cause: silence during an outage does more damage than the outage. State exactly what is impacted, what is not, what has been done so far, and when the next update comes. Never speculate on cause or blame a third party. Offer the workaround if one exists, and confirm the escalation contact on their side.

fields.label: Impact
fields.ph: e.g. the transaction service is degraded in one region

fields.label: Incident Reference
fields.ph: e.g. INC four four nine one

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Security Advisory & Patch
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: A critical vulnerability affects software they run and a fix is available. Be factual and calm: give the severity, whether it is known to be exploited, and the patch window you recommend. NEVER ask them to confirm credentials, versions of unrelated systems, or anything a social engineer would want — say plainly that you will not ask for such details, since a security call is exactly what an attacker would imitate. Direct them to the published advisory and offer a patching window.

fields.label: What's Affected
fields.ph: e.g. a component in the version you run

fields.label: Severity
fields.ph: e.g. rated critical, patch available now

fields.label: Recommended Action
fields.ph: e.g. apply the fix pack within 14 days

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Planned Change Window
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.desc: Confirm a maintenance or migration window
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: Confirm the agreed change window. Enterprise change is governed, so confirm the window, the expected outage, the rollback plan and who from their side is on the bridge. Check it does not collide with a freeze period such as a quarter end. A change that surprises their operations team is a change that gets escalated.

fields.label: Window
fields.ph: e.g. 11 at night to 3 in the morning

fields.label: What They Need Ready
fields.ph: e.g. change approval and a bridge contact

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Licence Compliance Evidence
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.desc: Deployment data needed for an entitlement review
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: An entitlement review needs deployment data from them. This is a sensitive conversation, so be scrupulously non-threatening: frame it as making sure they are correctly licensed and not over-paying, which is often the true outcome. Name exactly which reports are needed and by when. Never imply penalties or an audit finding, and route any dispute about entitlement to the account team rather than debating it.

fields.label: What's Needed
fields.ph: e.g. the deployment report from the last quarter

fields.label: Needed By
fields.ph: e.g. the end of the month

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Service Review (QBR)
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: Confirm the quarterly service review. Set the agenda in one line — availability against SLA, incident trends, and the roadmap for next quarter — so the right people attend rather than a delegate. Ask who else should be in the room, since the budget holder is often not the day-to-day contact.

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Cloud Consumption Review
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: Their consumption is drifting from their commitment — either burning it early or leaving it unused. Lead with the number and what it means for their bill, then the practical option: right-size, re-commit at a better rate, or shift workloads. Be honest when the recommendation reduces their spend, because that is what earns the next conversation.

fields.label: The Number
fields.ph: e.g. tracking 30 percent above your committed spend

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Invoice Due
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: A business call to accounts payable. Reference the invoice, PO and contract line, confirm it is approved and scheduled, and identify any blocker such as a missing PO or a milestone sign-off. Efficient and professional; never chase an operational contact for finance matters.

fields.label: Invoice / PO
fields.ph: e.g. invoice for Q2 managed services

IT Services & Enterprise Technology.label: Ticket Resolution Feedback
IT Services & Enterprise Technology.playbook: Ask two separate things: was the underlying problem actually fixed, and was the handling and communication good. A politely handled ticket that fixed nothing is still a failure, and in managed services that distinction drives renewal. If it is unresolved, reopen it on this call rather than logging a low score.

fields.label: About
fields.ph: e.g. the incident raised last week

Veterinary & Pet Care.label: Vaccination Due
Veterinary & Pet Care.playbook: Their pet's vaccination or booster is due. Use the pet's name throughout, which is what makes this call land. Lead with protection rather than the schedule, and book the appointment on the call. Mention if boarding or grooming requires it to be current.

Veterinary & Pet Care.label: Appointment Reminder
Veterinary & Pet Care.playbook: Confirm the appointment. Say whether the pet must fast beforehand and to bring any current medication. Owners are anxious before procedures, so be warm and reassuring, and make rescheduling easy.

fields.label: Preparation
fields.ph: e.g. no food after 10 PM the night before

Veterinary & Pet Care.label: Results / Discharge Update
Veterinary & Pet Care.desc: Test results in, or post-op update
Veterinary & Pet Care.playbook: Let the owner know results are in or share the agreed post-operative update. NEVER interpret a clinical result: that is the vet's call, and owners are emotionally invested. If they press, book the vet consultation. If the news is difficult, arrange for the vet to speak to them rather than delivering it yourself.

fields.label: Detail
fields.ph: e.g. the vet would like to discuss them

Veterinary & Pet Care.label: Wellness Plan Offer
Veterinary & Pet Care.desc: Preventive care plan or pet insurance
Veterinary & Pet Care.playbook: Offer the wellness plan. Anchor on the maths: routine care spread monthly usually costs less than paying per visit, and it means nothing gets skipped. Never use fear about their pet's health to sell, and make no promises about what the plan covers beyond the stated list.

fields.label: What's Included
fields.ph: e.g. vaccinations, two check-ups and flea treatment

Veterinary & Pet Care.label: Invoice Due
Veterinary & Pet Care.playbook: Remind them the treatment invoice is due. Be gentle: vet bills often follow a stressful episode and can be large. Give the amount and payment route, and mention any instalment option rather than letting it go unpaid.

Veterinary & Pet Care.label: Practice Feedback
Veterinary & Pet Care.playbook: Ask how the visit went for both the owner and the pet: waiting time, how the animal was handled, and whether the treatment was explained clearly. Capture a score and one comment. Route any concern about animal handling immediately.
